blocks.text: I can identify that all cells have some structures in common and I can explain that all organisms are unicellular or multicellular.

items.title: All living things are made of {cells}

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A living thing made of one or more cells.
The basic unit of all forms of life.
An organism made of many cells.
An organism that can only be viewed through a microscope.
An organism that consists of a single cell.

slides.title: Everything alive is made of cells

blocks.text: All organisms, including animals, plants, fungi and micro-organisms, are made up of one or more living cells.
Effectively, everything alive is made up of {cells}.
Some living organisms are multicellular. Some are unicellular. Tap each word to break it down.

items.root: multi = many, cellular = made of cells. So multicellular means made up of many cells.
uni = one, cellular = made of cells. So unicellular means made up of one cell.

blocks.text: Think of a unicycle: a bike with only one wheel. **Uni** means one.
Many animals and plants are multicellular. Most things that we see in everyday life are multicellular.
Their cells are organised in a hierarchy. The smallest part of an organism is always the cell.

items: Lots of similar cells work together to form a **tissue**.
Different tissues work together to form an **organ**, which has a specific job.
Several organs work together to form an **organ system**.
Different organ systems work together to form the whole **organism**.

slides.title: Plants have tissues and organs too

blocks.text: It is a mistake to think that only animals have tissues, organs and organ systems. Plants do too. Think about a plant:

items.title: Tissues
items.sub: different tissues make up the leaf

items.title: Organ system
items.sub: the root system or the shoot system

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Tissues are not only found in animals. Many multicellular organisms have tissues, for example mesophyll tissue in plants.
Micro-organisms such as bacteria are unicellular. They are made of just one cell.
E. coli bacteria are tiny rod-shaped organisms. Each rod is one whole organism, made of one cell. They are extremely small, so we need a microscope to see them.
**Unicellular** = one cell. **Multicellular** = many cells.
There are also unicellular organisms that are not bacteria. Phytoplankton are unicellular plant-like organisms. Amoeba are unicellular protists.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Bacteria are unicellular, but they are not the only unicellular organisms. So it is wrong to say that all unicellular organisms are bacteria.

blocks.q: Which of these is a unicellular organism that is not a bacterium?
blocks.why: An amoeba is a unicellular protist. E. coli is a bacterium and a rose bush is a multicellular plant.

blocks.q: Put each organism in the correct column.

items.def: Controls what enters and exits the cell. It is partially permeable: it lets some substances diffuse through but not others, which helps regulate the cell’s internal environment.
A jelly-like substance with dissolved nutrients and salts. It surrounds the sub-cellular structures and is where many chemical reactions essential to life take place.

Very small structures where protein synthesis takes place. Synthesis means to make.

blocks.label: Why don’t animal cells need chloroplasts?
blocks.text: Plants make glucose through photosynthesis, and this happens in the chloroplasts. Animals get their glucose from food and drink, so they do not need chloroplasts.

items: All organisms are made up of one or more living cells.
All cells have some structures in common and have a three-dimensional shape.
Chemical reactions essential to life occur in the cytoplasm, and the cell membrane regulates the cell’s internal environment.
Many animals and plants are multicellular: many cells organised to form tissues and organs.
Micro-organisms such as bacteria are unicellular: they are made of just one cell.

flashcards.back: A living thing made of one or more cells.
The basic unit of all forms of life.

An organism made of many cells.

multi = many

An organism that consists of a single cell.

uni = one (like a unicycle)

An organism that can only be viewed through a microscope.

Example: bacteria, which are unicellular.

No.

Phytoplankton are unicellular plant-like organisms and amoeba are unicellular protists.

flashcards.front: In a multicellular organism, what do lots of similar cells working together form?
flashcards.back:
A tissue.

Tissues form organs, organs form organ systems and organ systems form the organism.

flashcards.front: Which two structures do all cells have in common?
flashcards.back: The cell membrane and the cytoplasm.

flashcards.front: What does the cell membrane do?
flashcards.back:
It controls what enters and exits the cell.

It is partially permeable: it lets some substances through but not others.

A jelly-like substance containing dissolved nutrients and salts.

Many chemical reactions essential to life take place here.

flashcards.front: Which three structures do plant cells have that animal cells do not?
flashcards.back: The cell wall, chloroplasts and a large permanent vacuole.

flashcards.front: Where does aerobic respiration take place in a cell?
flashcards.back:
In the mitochondria (one is a mitochondrion).

A lot of energy is released.

flashcards.front: What is the job of the ribosomes?
flashcards.back: Protein synthesis: this is where proteins are made.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Cells
worksheet.instructions: Write a short answer to each question. Use the words from the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which structure of a plant cell contains chlorophyll and is where photosynthesis takes place?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which sub-cellular structures are where protein synthesis occurs?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are very small structures where proteins are made (synthesised).

questions.prompt: Which sub-cellular structure is where energy is released through aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration occurs in the mitochondria, releasing a lot of energy.

questions.prompt: Which sub-cellular structure contains DNA, which controls the activities of the cell?
questions.explanation: The nucleus contains the genetic information (DNA) that controls the cell’s activities.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the jelly-like substance in a cell where many chemical reactions take place?
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm contains dissolved nutrients and salts, and is where many chemical reactions essential to life take place.

questions.prompt: Which substance in the cell wall provides strength and support to the plant cell?
questions.explanation: The cell wall contains cellulose, which strengthens and supports the cell.

questions.prompt: A permanent ___ is a structure filled with cell sap that helps keep a plant cell turgid. Write the missing word.
questions.explanation: The permanent vacuole contains sap, which helps keep the cell turgid.

questions.prompt: Which structure controls what enters and exits the cell? (two words)
questions.explanation: The partially permeable cell membrane controls what enters and exits the cell.

questions.prompt: What word describes an organism that consists of a single cell?
questions.explanation: Uni means one, so unicellular organisms are made of one cell.

questions.prompt: What word describes an organism made of many cells?
questions.explanation: Multi means many, so multicellular organisms are made of many cells.

questions.prompt: In a multicellular organism, cells form tissues. Tissues form ___, which form organ systems. Write the missing word.
questions.explanation: The order is cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.

questions.prompt: How many cells is a bacterium made of? Write a number.
questions.explanation: Bacteria are unicellular: they are made of just one cell.
